title: git-cicd verdict is present and pending from the moment the workflow starts
body:
Unit 3 of plan `mdci-dev-6692` (record: `.pearls/docs/epics/mdci-dev-6692.md` in `mangimangi/medici-dev`). Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27: "I agree we should fix...I think pending w status write is ok".

## What happens today

The interface git-cicd was built to says: "One always-present check with a fixed name ... so anything waiting on 'checks pass' is never left hanging", and that "nothing ran" is never read as "passed". In v0.0.1 the check `git-cicd verdict` is the **last** thing to appear on a pull request. The generated workflow (`templates/workflow.yml`) is `decide`, then one runner per needed job, then `verdict`; GitHub creates a check run for a job only when that job is queued, and `verdict` is queued after the others finish. Between `decide` finishing and the job runners being queued, every check that exists on the commit is green.

That window was hit on the first repository to adopt git-cicd. On medici #177 (2026-11-27), medici's walker waited for the pull request's checks, saw "1 reported, none failed or pending" (the vendor-file check), and merged at about 16:15:40 UTC. `git-cicd decide` finished at 16:15:46; `unit-tests` and `toolchain-contract` started at 16:15:48; `git-cicd verdict` finished green at 16:20:24, four and a half minutes after the merge. Any reader that merges when no check is failing or pending can do the same on any repository that uses git-cicd.

The same window exists when no job is needed, and when `decide` itself has not started yet.

## Required behaviour

From the moment the git-cicd workflow starts on a pull request, something named `git-cicd verdict` is on the pull request's head commit and is **pending**, and it stays pending until the verdict is known. It then becomes success or failure exactly as the verdict is today (failed when a blocking job failed or could not run, or when the workflow does not match the config; otherwise passed, including when no job was needed). At no moment after the workflow has started is every check on the commit green while the verdict is still to come. A workflow run that is cancelled or superseded, or that dies before the verdict, does not leave `git-cicd verdict` green.

The owner accepted the cost: on the `open` moment the workflow's token may write commit statuses, as a narrow exception to "read-only on `open`". It gets that one write permission and no other; contents stay read-only. Nothing else about the interface changes: only the cron block of the generated file varies with the config; `verify` still compares the whole file; every fact about the change still reaches the tool as an environment variable.

A reader must not be shown two things of the same name that disagree: if both a status and a check run carry the name `git-cicd verdict`, they never show one green while the other is pending, and the documentation says which one a reader (a person, branch protection, a script that lists a pull request's checks) should rely on.

If this cannot be had with GitHub Actions as required, stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`) with what was found; do not ship something that narrows the window without closing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- On this issue's own pull request into `plan/mdci-dev-6692`, `git-cicd verdict` is pending on the head commit before git-cicd's `test` job has finished, and ends green; the pull request description gives the evidence (timestamps of the pending state and of the `test` job, read from the platform, not asserted).
- With no job needed (a change only to files in `needs_nothing`), `git-cicd verdict` is pending from the start of the run and ends green with the "0 of N jobs needed" text.
- When a blocking job fails, `git-cicd verdict` ends failed.
- The generated workflow grants, on the pull request trigger, the status-write permission and no other write permission; a test asserts the permissions block.
- Two configs that differ only in jobs that are not `cron` still generate the same file, and `verify` still fails on a hand edit.
- `README.md` says the verdict is present and pending from the start, names the permission and why, and says which object a reader should wait on.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; the checks on this issue's pull request are seen green, including `git-cicd verdict`, before the work is called done.
- git-cicd's own `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` is regenerated and committed with the change.

## Out of scope

The `merge` and `cron` moments and manual runs. Any change to git-vendored or git-semver, or to a vendor-protected file. Any change in medici or another consumer: they pick the fix up by installing the release and regenerating their workflow.

title: The pending git-cicd verdict is posted without waiting for a superseded run to be cancelled
body:
Follow-up to `gcd-f8eb` (git-cicd #5), unit 3 of plan `mdci-dev-6692`. This issue's branch starts from `gcd-f8eb/impl`, so its pull request contains #5 and replaces it. Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27.

## What happens today

With #5, `git-cicd verdict` is a commit status that the first step of the first job (`git-cicd decide`) sets to pending. #5 states: "Until that first step runs, the `git-cicd decide` check run is itself queued. So the commit never shows only green checks while the verdict is still to come."

That does not hold when a run is superseding an older one. The generated workflow has a workflow-level `concurrency` group per pull request with `cancel-in-progress` on pull requests, so a newer run waits, with no job created and therefore no check run and no status, until the older run has been cancelled.

This is what was hit on medici #177 (2026-11-27), read from `GET /repos/mangimangi/medici/actions/runs/46032007325/jobs` and the run list:

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 16:14:53 | git-cicd run 46031961919 created on `f090b1d` |
| 16:15:10 | a second push; git-cicd run 46032007325 created on `450267a`; Check Vendor Files run created |
| 16:15:21 | `check` (Check Vendor Files, a separate workflow) completed, success |
| 16:15:37 | run 46031961919 finished cancelling; **`git-cicd decide` job of run 46032007325 created** |
| 16:15:39 | `git-cicd decide` started |
| ~16:15:40 | medici's walker, having read "1 reported, none failed or pending", merged the pull request |
| 16:20:24 | the verdict, green |

From 16:15:21 to 16:15:37 the head commit had exactly one check, and it was green. A pending status posted by the first step of `decide` would have appeared at about 16:15:40.

## Required behaviour

When a git-cicd run starts for a head commit, the pending `git-cicd verdict` status is posted without waiting for any other run of the workflow to finish or be cancelled. Superseding is kept where it saves work: a newer push still cancels the older run's jobs that run the repository's scripts. A superseded or cancelled run never turns the newer commit's status green, and never leaves its own commit's status green without a verdict. Everything #5 established stays: one object named `git-cicd verdict`, the status; `statuses: write` only on the jobs that post it; only the cron block of the generated file varies; `verify` compares the whole file.

`README.md` is corrected where it repeats the claim above: it says what a reader can rely on and from when, including the superseding case, and does not promise more than the platform gives (the short time between a push and GitHub creating the run is the platform's).

If GitHub Actions cannot post the status ahead of the concurrency wait, stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`) with what was tried.

## Acceptance criteria

- Shown on this issue's own pull request, with times read from the platform and given in the pull request description: two pushes to the pull request less than 30 seconds apart; for the second run, the time the run was created, the time its status-posting job was created, and the time `git-cicd verdict` became pending on the second head commit. The pending status is there within a few seconds of the run being created, not after the first run has finished cancelling.
- In that same sequence the first run's script-running job is cancelled (superseding still works), and the first commit's `git-cicd verdict` does not end green unless its verdict really was reached.
- The second commit's `git-cicd verdict` ends green.
- A test asserts where the concurrency group is and is not in the generated workflow, and the permissions block is unchanged from #5 (status write on the posting jobs only).
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; git-cicd's own `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` is regenerated and committed; the checks and the status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

Readers of checks (`madp pr checks`, medici's merge step): they are other repositories' work. The `merge` and `cron` moments and manual runs. Any vendor-protected file.

title: Checks say whose they are: a job's display name, repo:job rows, and owner@version per step in the report
body:
Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27. The owner: "would be nice if the git-cicd checks had format `<human readable name> / <owning repo>:<job name>:<step name>`", and "owning repo should incl version...it should be clear jobs repo version".

## What happens today

On a pull request in a repository that uses git-cicd v0.0.2 (medici, for example) the rows are `git-cicd decide`, one row per job named with the bare job name from the config (`unit-tests`, `toolchain-contract`), and `git-cicd report`, each shown by GitHub after the workflow's name (`git-cicd / unit-tests`), plus the commit status `git-cicd verdict`. A job has no display name: `templates/workflow.yml` names the script-running job `${{ matrix.job }}`. A step is named only in the report, and only when it fails (`failed (step <step>, exit <code>)`). Nothing says which repository a step's script belongs to, or which version of a vendored tool ran.

## Required behaviour

1. **A job may declare a display name**, the optional field `name` in the config (a short human-readable string). It is validated like every other field; a job without one behaves as if its `name` were its job name. `README.md`, `templates/config.schema` and the default config template know the field.

2. **Rows are stable and say whose job it is.** The script-running job's row is `<name> / <repo>:<job>`, where `<repo>` is the name of the repository the workflow runs in (for example `Unit tests / medici:unit-tests`). No version appears in a row name: a row name is what branch protection and anything else that waits on a check refers to, and it must not change when a tool is upgraded. `git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd report` and the status `git-cicd verdict` keep their names.

3. **The report names every step, with its owner and the owner's version.** For each job the report has one line per step that ran (and setup), in the form `<name> / <owner>@<version>:<job>:<step>`, with its result and its time; the job's own line stays. `<step>` is the step's file name. `<owner>` is the vendor when the step's file is under `.vendored/pkg/<vendor>/`, with `<version>` read from `.vendored/manifests/<vendor>.version`; otherwise the owner is the repository itself, with the version from the version file the repository's git-semver config names (`.vendored/configs/git-semver.json`, `version_file`, default `VERSION`) when that file exists. An owner with no version is shown without `@<version>`; a version is never guessed. The verdict status's description stays within the platform's length limit; the step lines belong to the report.

4. **A pull request tests a change, not a release.** The report's header gives the short head commit, so the repository's own version (the last release) is not read as the version of the change under test.

5. The same names appear in a local run (`git-cicd check`), where the repository's name comes from the checkout (say how, and what is shown when it cannot be found).

The injection rules hold: a display name is data. It reaches the workflow only through the decide job's outputs and environment variables, never spliced into a command line, and a name containing quotes, `$`, backticks or a newline is either refused at validation or shown literally and runs nothing. Only the cron block of the generated file varies with the config; `verify` still compares the whole file.

If the row name cannot carry the display name without the generated file varying with the config, stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`).

## Acceptance criteria

- A config with `"name"` on a job validates; a `name` that is not a non-empty single-line string is refused with the job and the reason; a job without `name` is unchanged apart from the new row format.
- On this issue's own pull request, git-cicd's own job shows as `<name> / git-cicd:test` (its config gains a `name`), read from the platform and quoted in the pull request description.
- The report for a job with a repository step and a step under `.vendored/pkg/<vendor>/` shows both lines with the right owner and version; tests cover a vendored owner with a manifest version, a vendored owner without one, the repository with a version file, and the repository without one.
- A test shows a display name with shell metacharacters reaches the report unaltered and runs nothing.
- Two configs that differ only in jobs that are not `cron` (their `name` included) still generate the same workflow file.
- `README.md` documents the field, the row format, the report's step lines and where each version comes from.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` is regenerated and committed if the template changed; the checks and the `git-cicd verdict` status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

A row or a status per step. Versions in row names. The `merge` and `cron` moments and manual runs. Any vendor-protected file. Consumers: they pick this up by installing the release and regenerating their workflow.

title: git-cicd's own rows and status follow the naming pattern; one workflow per moment, named for it; title-case names
body:
Follow-up to `gcd-8b02` (git-cicd #8). This issue's branch starts from `gcd-8b02/impl`, so its pull request contains #8 and replaces it. Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27, after seeing #8's rows on the platform.

## What happens today (with #8)

On a pull request the rows are, as GitHub shows them: `git-cicd / git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd / Unit tests / git-cicd:test`, `git-cicd / git-cicd report`, and the status `git-cicd verdict`.

- The job rows follow `<name> / <repo>:<job>`; `git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd report` and the status `git-cicd verdict` do not. The owner: "how come decide, verdict and report don't follow the naming pattern?" (The planning session had told #8 to leave them.)
- GitHub puts the workflow's name before every row, and the one generated workflow is named `git-cicd` for every moment. The owner: "I see git-cicd before the human readable name".
- A job without `name` shows its bare job name (`unit-tests`), and git-cicd's own config says `"name": "Unit tests"`. The owner: "the human readable name should be title case".
- There is one generated file, `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml`, for all four moments. Permissions by moment (read-only on `open`; write on `merge`, `cron` and manual) and the overlap rules (`open` superseded; `merge` queued, never cancelled) would all be conditions inside it.

## Required behaviour

1. **git-cicd's own rows and status follow the pattern, with git-cicd as their owner.** The deciding job's row is `Decide / git-cicd:decide`, the reporting job's is `Report / git-cicd:report`, and the commit status is `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`. Everything #5 and #6 established about the status holds under its new name: one object carries the name; pending from the first step of the first job, without waiting on a superseded run; final from the last step of the report job; a cancelled or superseded run never leaves it green.

2. **One generated workflow per moment, named for the moment.** The workflow for the `open` moment is named `Open`, so a row reads `Open / Unit Tests / medici:unit-tests`. The names for the others are `Merge`, `Cron` and `Manual`; the owner chose the moment words over `CI`/`CD` because the config already says `"on": ["open"]` and a moment is not a kind of job. Each moment's workflow is its own file with its own trigger, its own permissions stated at the top level or per job, and its own overlap rule. **Only the `open` file is generated in this issue**, because only `open` executes; the generator, `verify`, the README and the tests are shaped so that adding the `merge`, `cron` and manual files later adds files and changes none. Choose the file names once, so no adopter has to rename a file again, and record them. The rule "only the cron block varies with the config" becomes: every generated file is fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block.

3. **The old single file goes.** `generate` in a repository that has `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` writes the new file and removes the old one; `verify` fails, naming the command to run, while the old file is still there or the new one is missing or different. `install.sh` lists the generated workflow files as editable for the vendor check in a way that covers the files to come. git-cicd's own repository is migrated in this issue.

4. **Title case, by convention and by default, never by rewriting.** A job without `name` is shown under a name derived from its job name: `-` and `_` become spaces and each word is capitalised (`unit-tests` shows as `Unit Tests`). A `name` a repository wrote is shown exactly as written; git-cicd does not change its case (`PyPI`, `mypy`). git-cicd's own config and every example in the README, the schema description and the tests use title case.

Everything else stands: rows carry no version; the report's step lines are `<name> / <owner>@<version>:<job>:<step>`; a display name is data and runs nothing; `statuses: write` only on the jobs that post the status and no other write permission on `open`.

If GitHub does not allow something here as required (for example a row or status name in this form), stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`) with what was tried.

## Acceptance criteria

- On this issue's own pull request, read from the platform and quoted in the description: the check runs `Decide / git-cicd:decide`, `Unit Tests / git-cicd:test` and `Report / git-cicd:report`, under the workflow named `Open`; the commit status `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`, pending before the test job finishes and ending success; no check or status named `git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd report` or `git-cicd verdict` on the head commit.
- `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` no longer exists in this repository; the `open` workflow file does and is the generator's output; `verify` passes, and fails in a test when the old file is present.
- A job without `name` is shown as its job name in title case, in the row and in the report; a job with `name` is shown exactly as written (tests for both, including a mixed-case name).
- Two configs that differ only in jobs that are not `cron` generate the same files.
- A test asserts the `open` workflow's permissions: status write on the two posting jobs only, nothing on the job that runs scripts.
- `README.md` describes the per-moment workflows and their names, the file names, the migration from the single file (`generate`, commit the new file and the deletion), the rows and the status under their new names, and which object a reader waits on.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; the checks and the status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

Executing `merge`, `cron` or manual runs, and generating their files. A row or status per step. Versions in row names. Any vendor-protected file. Consumers: medici names `git-cicd verdict` in its docs and has `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml`; it migrates when it installs the release, in its own repository.

title: Moments are called triggers: CICD_TRIGGER, --trigger, and the docs
body:
Follow-up to `gcd-f7ce` (git-cicd #9). This issue's branch starts from `gcd-f7ce/impl`, so its pull request contains #8 and #9 and replaces both. The owner, 2026-11-27: "moment is really trigger...is it too late to change that?"

## What happens today

git-cicd calls `open`, `merge`, `cron` and a manual run "moments". The word is not in a repository's config (the field is `on`), but it is everywhere else: about 95 places in `git-cicd`, `README.md`, the workflow templates and the tests. Two of them are public: the environment variable `CICD_MOMENT` every setup and step script receives, and the `--moment` option of `decide`, `run-job` and `report`. Messages say "the <moment> moment is not built yet". Nothing outside this repository depends on the word yet: medici, the only adopter, does not read `CICD_MOMENT` and does not use the term.

## Required behaviour

The word is "trigger" everywhere a person or a script meets it, and nothing is left that says "moment" in this sense:

- Scripts receive `CICD_TRIGGER`; `CICD_MOMENT` is no longer set.
- The commands take `--trigger`; `--moment` is not accepted.
- Messages, the report, the README, the schema descriptions, comments in the generated workflows, and the code's own identifiers and tests use "trigger" ("the merge trigger is not built yet").
- No alias and no deprecation path: the owner chose not to keep a second name, because nothing uses the first.

Nothing else changes: the config field stays `on` with the values `open`, `merge`, `cron`; the workflows are still named `Open`, `Merge`, `Cron`, `Manual`, one file per trigger; rows, the `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` status, permissions and the generated file names are as #9 left them. If the generated workflow's text changes, it is regenerated and committed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `git grep -i moment` in this repository finds nothing in `git-cicd`, `README.md`, `templates/`, `tests/`, `ci/`, `install.sh` or `.github/workflows/` that uses the word for a trigger (an ordinary English use, if any is left, is listed in the pull request description).
- A test shows a step receives `CICD_TRIGGER=open` and that `CICD_MOMENT` is absent from its environment.
- `--moment` is rejected as an unknown option; `--trigger` works on every command that took `--moment`.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; `verify` passes; the checks and the `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

Any change of behaviour. The tracker's and planning documents' history under `.pearls/` (they record what was said at the time). Executing `merge`, `cron` or manual runs.

title: A run that needs no job shows a skipped row named with raw ${{ }} text
body:
Part of plan `git-dev-883c`, delivering into `plan/git-dev-883c` (this issue replaces `gcd-4674`, which was filed from `main` before the coverage gate existed). Found while running the plan (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`), on git-cicd pull request #13.

## What happens today

When a run needs no job, the job that would run the config's scripts is skipped, and GitHub shows its row under the raw text of its `name:` expression instead of a readable name:

```
${{ fromJSON(needs.decide.outputs.names)[matrix.job] }} / ${{ github.event.repository.name }}:${{ matrix.job }}
```

Seen on 2026-11-28: the push of branch `claude/git-tools-cicd-migration-mehnbq` started the `Merge` workflow (run 46091911411); no job has that branch in `branches`, so `decide` reported nothing needed, and the skipped `run` job appeared on pull request #13 as check run 140814563245, conclusion `skipped`, with the name above.

The cause is in every workflow template: the `run` job has `if: needs.decide.outputs.any == 'true'` and a `name:` built from the matrix (`templates/workflows/open.yml` line 127, `merge.yml` line 145, `cron.yml` line 123, `manual.yml` line 160). GitHub does not expand a matrix job's name when the job is skipped before its matrix is evaluated.

It was rare while only `open` existed. With the `merge` trigger it happens on every push to any branch that no `merge` job names, in every repository that adopts git-cicd, and each such row shows on the commit and on any open pull request for that branch.

## Required behaviour

A run that needs no job shows no row with unexpanded `${{ }}` text, on any trigger. What it shows instead (no row at all for the skipped job, or one readable fixed name) is for the implementer to decide and document; the rows of jobs that do run keep the `<name> / <repo>:<job>` form, and no existing row or status name changes (`Decide / git-cicd:decide`, `Report / git-cicd:report`, `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`, and config job rows).

The generated workflows stay fixed text (only the cron schedule block varies), `generate` and `verify` cover the change, and the committed `.github/workflows/git-cicd-*.yml` are regenerated in the same pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- On a pull request into `plan/**` or `main`, a push that needs no `merge` job produces no check run whose name contains `${{`. Shown on the unit's own pull request: list the check runs of its head commit.
- The same holds for `open` when only `needs_nothing` files change, and the templates for `cron` and manual runs are changed the same way.
- A run that needs jobs still shows one row per needed job named `<name> / <repo>:<job>`, and the verdict status is unchanged.
- `./git-cicd verify` passes; `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; the tests cover the template change.
- The README says what a run that needs nothing shows.

title: install.sh lists generated workflows in its manifest, so they are both the repository's to commit and protected
body:
Part of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`), added by the owner on 2026-11-28 from a consumer's note (`mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/consumer-note-git-cicd-v0.0.3-and-v0.0.4-in-medici.md`). Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## What happens today

git-cicd tells a repository two different things about the workflows it generates.

- The README and `generate` say they are the repository's to commit: "Whoever upgrades git-cicd or changes the config runs `generate` and commits what it writes in the same pull request", and the installed config lists `.github/workflows/git-cicd-*.yml` as editable (`_vendor.allowed`, `templates/config.json`).
- `install.sh` lists every generated workflow in the manifest it hands to git-vendored (lines 86-93: after `generate`, each existing `.github/workflows/git-cicd-<trigger>.yml` is added to `INSTALLED_FILES`). git-vendored treats every manifest path as a protected vendor file unless the vendor's `allowed` list matches it.

So the same file is "yours to commit" and "protected". It only works while the repository's registry happens to allow the pattern. In medici, which registered git-cicd at v0.0.2, the registry allowed only `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml`; a session that ran `generate` as instructed was rejected by `.vendored/check` with "Protected vendor files were modified: .github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml", and the workflow had to be repaired by hand from a branch named like an install branch.

The manifest also names files an install pull request does not deliver: git-vendored leaves workflow files out of an install pull request pushed with the workflow's own token. In git-semver and git-vendored after installing v0.0.4, `.vendored/manifests/git-cicd.files` listed `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml` and `git-cicd-manual.yml`, none of which was on `main`.

## Required behaviour

One answer, agreed with the owner: the repository generates and commits the generated workflows; they are allowed, never protected.

- `install.sh` does not list `.github/workflows/git-cicd-<trigger>.yml` in the manifest. The manifest holds what git-cicd owns: the tool, the templates under the install directory, and the schema.
- `install.sh` still runs `generate` on every install, so a first install and an upgrade leave the right workflows on disk for whoever commits them, and still removes the old single `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml`.
- The installed config still lists `.github/workflows/git-cicd-*.yml` as allowed.
- The README ("Installing", "What lands where", "The generate/verify rule") says the one answer plainly: who owns the generated workflows, that an install pull request may arrive without them (when it is pushed with a token that may not write workflow files), and that the fix is `generate` and a commit from any branch, which the vendor check accepts.

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing.

## Acceptance criteria

- After `install.sh` runs in a test repository with `VENDOR_MANIFEST` set, the manifest lists no path under `.github/workflows/`, and the generated workflows exist on disk.
- The tests (pytest or bats) show that for a first install and for an upgrade from a version that listed them.
- `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; `./git-cicd verify` passes; the generated workflows of this repository are unchanged.
- The README has one statement of who owns generated workflows, and no sentence that says they are protected.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: A manual run is started from a form that lists the jobs and their inputs
Generate the Manual workflow's form from the config (job dropdown, one field per input, validate and verify)
body:
Epic gcd-8f83, part 1 of 3 (planning doc `.pearls/docs/epics/gcd-8f83.md`, "What ships", first item). Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## Context (re-validated against the code on 2026-11-28)

The Manual workflow template `templates/workflows/manual.yml` is fixed text: `workflow_dispatch` (lines 74-85) asks for two free-text fields, `job` (type string) and `inputs` (a JSON object of strings). Its header comment says "Every generated file is fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block; this file does not vary with the config at all" (lines 13-15) and "The file cannot list a job's inputs, since it does not vary with the config" (lines 27-28). In `git-cicd`: `render_workflow(config, tool, template)` (line ~1011) replaces only `__SCHEDULE__\n` (built by `schedule_block(config)`, line ~1001, which writes each cron with `json.dumps`) and `__TOOL__`; `rendered_triggers`/`stale_paths`/`render_workflows`/`verify_workflow` (lines ~1024-1104) decide which files are generated and compare them whole. Inputs are validated by `_validate_inputs` (line ~211; `INPUT_NAME_RE = ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, `INPUT_FIELDS = description, required, default, choices`; description already single-line printable) and jobs by `_validate_job`/`validate_config` (lines ~332-520; normalized job has `manual` = `job.get("manual", True) is not False`).

The decision (agreed, do not reopen): the Manual workflow varies with the config, as the cron workflow's schedule block does. Only the Manual workflow changes; `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml` and `git-cicd-cron.yml` must stay byte-identical (their templates are not edited, including their header comments).

## Scope

1. `templates/workflows/manual.yml`: replace the fixed `inputs:` block under `workflow_dispatch` with a placeholder (e.g. `__FORM__`) that `render_workflow` fills from the config, the same way `__SCHEDULE__` is filled for cron. Update this template's header comment to state the new rule: the generated files are fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block and the Manual workflow's form; whoever changes a job's inputs or adds/removes a manual job runs `generate` and commits.
2. A `form_block(config)` (name free) that writes, in config order of `config["jobs"]`:
   - `job`: `type: choice`, `required: true`, `options:` the names of the jobs whose normalized `manual` is true, in config order, with a description. Job names are already validated identifiers (`JOB_NAME_RE`).
   - one field per distinct declared input name of those jobs, in first-seen order (config order of jobs, then declaration order of inputs). Each field carries the declaration's description, its default, and for an input with `choices` `type: choice` with `options:` the choices (a dropdown); otherwise `type: string`.
   - every generated input field is `required: false` in the form, since the form shows every job's fields at once; the tool keeps enforcing `required` for the chosen job (decision, see below).
   - when a field is not used by every manual job, its description says which jobs use it (e.g. `Version bump type (job release)`; exact wording free, but stable and tested).
   - every description, default and option is written with `json.dumps` (a JSON string is a valid YAML double-quoted scalar), exactly as `schedule_block` writes cron expressions. Input names are written bare (they match `INPUT_NAME_RE`).
3. Sharing: an input declared by more than one manual job under one name appears once. `validate` refuses (as a `ConfigError` line) declarations of one name that cannot share a field: different `choices` (including one with choices and one without) or different `default` (an absent default and `""` count as different only if the implementer documents it; decision: treat absent and `""` as the same, since both give the empty string to the script, see `input_values`). The message names the input and the jobs, and what to change (e.g. `input bump_type is declared by jobs release and other with different choices; give them the same choices and default, or rename one`). Differing descriptions are allowed: the field uses the first job's description (decision; descriptions do not change the value a script gets).
4. Reserved name: `validate` refuses an input named `job` on a job that allows manual runs (it would collide with the form's `job` field), naming the job.
5. Platform limit: GitHub allows at most 25 inputs in a `workflow_dispatch` workflow (GitHub changelog 2025-12-04 "Actions workflow_dispatch workflows now support 25 inputs"; was 10). Re-check the current limit in GitHub's documentation when implementing and put the source in a code comment next to the constant (e.g. `MANUAL_FORM_LIMIT = 25`). The `job` field counts, so at most 24 distinct input fields. `validate` refuses a config whose form would exceed it, with the count and the limit and what to change (fewer distinct input names, or `"manual": false` on a job).
6. No job allows a manual run: `generate` does not write `.github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml` (and removes it when present), and `verify` fails while it is still there, naming `generate` — the same treatment as the cron workflow when no job has cron (`rendered_triggers`, `stale_paths`, the "is still there" message in `verify_workflow`). Reason: a `choice` input needs at least one option, and a Manual workflow with nothing to run must not exist, mirroring cron. The `job` field's dropdown is never empty.
7. `verify` covers the form like the schedule block: since `verify_workflow` regenerates and compares whole files, adding or changing an input, adding a manual job or setting `"manual": false` without regenerating fails `verify` with the diff and `run: <tool> generate and commit ...`.
8. `templates/config.schema`: update the `jobs` description for inputs (named fields in the Manual workflow's form, shared by name across jobs, the `job` reserved name, the form limit). Leave the sentence about how values are given (`a manual run gives values as a JSON object in the Manual workflow's inputs field`) for gcd-8f83.2 to rewrite, or rewrite it here if this lands after it.

Out of scope here (other issues of this epic): how the tool reads the form's values on a run and the removal of the free-text `inputs` field and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` (gcd-8f83.2; until then the template keeps the `inputs` free-text field as the last field and its env lines unchanged, so a run still works); hostile-declaration tests (gcd-8f83.2); regenerating this repo's own workflow, README and AGENTS.md (gcd-8f83.3). Not in scope: one workflow per job, `key=value` input, any change to `open`/`merge`/`cron`.

## Decisions recorded

- Fields are `required: false` in the form and required-ness stays enforced by the tool for the chosen job: a `required: true` field would force the owner to fill inputs of jobs they did not choose.
- Absent default and `""` are the same default for sharing: both give the script the empty string.
- Differing descriptions of a shared input do not refuse the config; the first job's description is used, plus the "used by" note.
- An input named `job` is refused for manual jobs (collides with the `job` field).
- Limit 25 including `job`; source in a code comment.
- No manual job: no Manual workflow file (mirrors cron), verify flags a stale one.

## Tests (pytest, following `tests/test_workflow.py` and `tests/test_config.py` patterns)

- The form for a config with two manual jobs and one `"manual": false` job: `job` options list exactly the manual jobs in config order; each input appears once, with description, default, and `type: choice` + `options` for choices; the "used by" note appears only on fields not used by every manual job. Parse the generated file with a small YAML-subset check or exact-text comparison (no new dependency; standard library only).
- A shared input with identical declarations appears once; differing choices and differing defaults are each refused with a message naming the input and both jobs.
- An input named `job` on a manual job is refused; on a `"manual": false` job it is allowed.
- 24 distinct inputs pass; 25 are refused with `25` and the limit in the message.
- No manual job: `generate` writes no manual file and removes an existing one; `verify` fails while it exists and names `generate`.
- `verify` fails after an input is added or changed without `generate`, naming the command, and passes after `generate`.
- `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` rendered for a config are byte-identical to what the current templates give (a test pinning that `render_workflow` of those templates is unaffected by inputs/manual flags).
- Coverage of `git-cicd` stays at 99% or more (`./git-cicd check --job test`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `./git-cicd generate` writes a Manual workflow whose `job` is a dropdown of the manual jobs in config order and whose other fields are the declared inputs, once each, with description, default and, for choices, a dropdown.
- `validate` refuses incompatible shared declarations, an input named `job` on a manual job and a form over the platform limit, each naming what to change.
- With no manual job no Manual workflow is generated, and `verify` fails while a stale one exists.
- `verify` fails when the form and the config disagree, naming `generate`.
- Open, Merge and Cron workflows are byte-identical to before.
- `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing (no vendor-protected file touched).

title: Read manual inputs from the form's named fields only; remove the free-text inputs field; hostile-declaration tests
body:
Epic gcd-8f83, part 2 of 3 (planning doc `.pearls/docs/epics/gcd-8f83.md`, "What ships", second item). Depends on gcd-8f83.1 (the form generated from the config). Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## Context (re-validated against the code on 2026-11-28)

Today the Manual workflow (`templates/workflows/manual.yml`) has a free-text `inputs` field (lines 81-85) passed as `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS: ${{ inputs.inputs }}` to the decide step (line 148) and the run step (line 190). In `git-cicd`: `MANUAL_INPUTS_ENV = "CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS"` (line ~75), `parse_manual_inputs(text)` (line ~277, JSON object of strings), `input_values(job, given)` (line ~294: refuses an undeclared key, a value outside choices, a missing required input when `given` is not None; else default, else `""`), `manual_input_values(job)` (line ~324), used by `decide_manual` (line ~634, via `manual_refusal` at line ~618) and `run_job` (line ~902, manual branch at ~910-916, which raises `UsageError("manual run refused: ...")`). `script_env` (line ~861) sets one `CICD_INPUT_<NAME>` per declared input and strips inherited `CICD_INPUT_` variables and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS`. Injection rules (README "No accidental injection"): form values reach the tool and scripts only as environment variables, never on a command line and never as `${{ }}` inside a `run:` block.

## Scope

1. Remove the free-text `inputs` field from the Manual workflow's form and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` from the tool. The decide and run steps instead set one fixed env line, `CICD_MANUAL_FORM: ${{ toJSON(inputs) }}` (name free, but one variable; decision below), so the env blocks stay fixed text and no form value appears in a `run:` block. The tool reads manual values on one path only: a replacement for `parse_manual_inputs`/`manual_input_values` that reads `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` (a JSON object of strings from the form; the `job` key is ignored, since the job comes from `--job`), then gives the chosen job's declared inputs to `input_values`. `MANUAL_INPUTS_ENV`, `parse_manual_inputs` and their tests go; `script_env` strips `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` instead of `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS`.
2. A run passes only the fields of the chosen job to it. A field the chosen job does not declare is ignored, not an error, since the form shows every job's fields: when its value differs from the field's form default (the declared default; else the first choice for a dropdown, which GitHub preselects; else `""`) the decision records it and the report says so (e.g. `ignored input vendor (job release does not declare it)`); a field left at its default is ignored silently. `decide_manual` and `run_job` agree (the same function).
3. Required inputs: an empty value from the form for a required input of the chosen job counts as missing, and the run is refused with `job <name>: input <key> is required` (the form cannot mark it required, see gcd-8f83.1). A value outside its choices is still refused. Refusals keep today's shape: decide records the reason, needs no job, the report is FAILED with it; `run-job` exits 2.
4. Locally (`decide --trigger manual`, `run-job --trigger manual`) the same variable is read; without it every input is its default (required inputs refused).
5. Hostile declarations: names written into the generated file are validated identifiers (`JOB_NAME_RE`, `INPUT_NAME_RE`); descriptions, defaults and choice values are written with `json.dumps` (gcd-8f83.1). Add `validate` refusal of `${{` in a description, default or choice of a job that allows manual runs, naming the job and input — decision: GitHub evaluates `${{ }}` in workflow strings and YAML has no escape for it, so refusing is the only way to guarantee it is not evaluated. Defaults and choices with a newline are written escaped by `json.dumps` (`\n`) and stay one line.
6. Update the Manual template's header comment (lines 21-33) for the new event and reading path.

## Tests (pytest in `tests/test_workflow.py`, `tests/test_decide.py`, `tests/test_run.py`, `tests/test_config.py`)

- Hostile-declaration test: generate from a config whose descriptions, defaults and choices contain `'`, `"`, `:`, `#`, `$`, backticks, `\n` (defaults/choices), `{{` and leading/trailing spaces; show the file is still one well-formed workflow (the `workflow_dispatch.inputs` keys are exactly the expected names, each value round-trips with `json.loads` of the written scalar) and that no `run:` block in any generated file (open, merge, cron, manual) contains any value taken from the config. `${{` in each of description/default/choice is refused by `validate`.
- `decide --trigger manual` and `run-job --trigger manual` with `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` set: the chosen job gets its inputs as `CICD_INPUT_<NAME>` (a step script prints its env); a value with quotes, `$`, backticks and a newline reaches the script literally.
- A non-default value for a field of another job is ignored and reported; a default one is ignored silently.
- Missing/empty required input, value outside choices, malformed `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` (not JSON, not an object of strings) are refused with the reason in the report.
- `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` and inherited `CICD_INPUT_*` do not reach scripts.
- The template has no `inputs` free-text field and no `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS`.
- Coverage of `git-cicd` stays at 99% or more.

## Decisions recorded

- One env variable `CICD_MANUAL_FORM: ${{ toJSON(inputs) }}` rather than one env line per field: keeps the step env blocks fixed text (only the form varies), one reading path, values only in an env var.
- Ignored fields are reported only when they differ from the field's form default; otherwise every run would report every other job's prefilled defaults.
- An empty value for a required input is missing.
- `${{` refused in manual jobs' descriptions, defaults and choices.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Manual form has no free-text `inputs` field; the tool has one path for reading manual values.
- A manual run with fields set gives the chosen job its inputs as `CICD_INPUT_<NAME>`, shown by tests for `decide` and `run-job` on the manual trigger; values reach a script literally.
- Undeclared fields are ignored and reported when non-default; refusals (required, choices, malformed) still report the reason.
- Hostile-declaration tests pass; no `run:` block in any generated file contains a value taken from the config.
- `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` byte-identical to before the epic.
- `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: Regenerate git-cicd's own Manual form and document the form in README and AGENTS.md
body:
Epic gcd-8f83, part 3 of 3 (planning doc `.pearls/docs/epics/gcd-8f83.md`, "What ships", third item). Depends on gcd-8f83.1 and gcd-8f83.2. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## Context (re-validated against the code on 2026-11-28)

`.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` (editable vendor config, not vendor-protected) declares `test` (open), `release` (merge on main; inputs `bump_type` choices patch/minor/major default patch, `subdirectory` default "", `changelog_description` default ""), `vendor-check` (open) and `update-vendored` (cron `0 9 * * 1` on main; inputs `vendor` default all, `version` default latest, `private` choices true/false default false). No job sets `manual`, so all four allow manual runs today (`manual` defaults to true).

## Scope

1. Config: set `"manual": false` on `test` and `vendor-check` in `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`, so the form's `job` dropdown is exactly `release` and `update-vendored` as the epic's acceptance criteria require. Decision: AGENTS.md says the owner starts only `release` and `update-vendored` by hand; the open jobs run on pull requests.
2. Run `./git-cicd generate` and commit `.github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml`. It must have a `job` dropdown with `release` and `update-vendored` and the named fields `bump_type` (dropdown patch, minor, major; default patch), `subdirectory`, `changelog_description`, `vendor` (default all), `version` (default latest) and `private` (dropdown true, false; default false), each with its description and default, and a note of the job using it (none is shared). `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` unchanged byte for byte.
3. `tests/test_own_jobs.py`: assert the generated form for this repo's config (the job options and the six fields with descriptions, defaults and choices).
4. `README.md`:
   - "The generated workflows" (line ~384; the manual bullets at ~460-480 now describe two free-text fields, `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` and `-f inputs='{"bump_type": "minor"}'`): state the changed rule — the generated files are fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block and the Manual workflow's form (which jobs are listed, which fields, how shared names and the limit work); show the form an adopter gets (an example `workflow_dispatch` block); `gh workflow run git-cicd-manual.yml --ref main -f job=release -f bump_type=minor`; no Manual workflow when no job allows manual runs.
   - "The config" / "Declared inputs" (lines ~101-157; "Giving values" at ~138-143 and "Failures" at ~148-157 describe the JSON `inputs` field): rewrite for named fields, shared names, the `job` reserved name, `${{` refusal, the form limit (25 including `job`), ignored fields reported, required enforced by the tool.
   - Say that changing a job's inputs, adding a manual job or changing `manual` means `generate` and a commit in the same pull request (verify fails otherwise).
   - An upgrade note for adopters coming from a version with the two free-text fields: regenerate and commit; `-f inputs=...` and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` no longer exist; jobs that should not appear in the dropdown set `"manual": false`; anything scripting `gh workflow run ... -f inputs=` switches to one `-f <name>=<value>` per input.
   - "Developing git-cicd" (line ~690; the manual-run text at ~700-707 with `{"bump_type": "minor"}`): how the owner starts `release` or `update-vendored` by hand now (pick the job, fill the named fields); `test` and `vendor-check` are not manual.
   - Check the "Commands" table (line ~674) and "No accidental injection" (line ~229) for anything mentioning the JSON field.
5. `AGENTS.md` ("This repository's jobs" and "Vendored tools"): replace "the `inputs` field as JSON (for example `{"bump_type": "minor"}` or `{"vendor": "mangimangi/git-semver"}`; empty for the defaults)" with the named fields (job `release` with `bump_type` etc., job `update-vendored` with `vendor` etc.), and mention that a change to a job's inputs regenerates the Manual workflow.
6. Template header comments: only `templates/workflows/manual.yml` (done in gcd-8f83.1 and gcd-8f83.2; check it matches the README). The comments of `open.yml`, `merge.yml` and `cron.yml` ("Every generated file is fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block", line 13) are NOT changed, because those generated files must stay byte-identical (decision; the README carries the rule).

No vendor-protected file is added, changed or deleted; `.vendored/install` is not run.

## Acceptance criteria

- The committed `.github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml` matches `./git-cicd generate` and has the `job` dropdown `release`, `update-vendored` and the fields `bump_type` (patch, minor, major), `subdirectory`, `changelog_description`, `vendor`, `version`, `private`, each with its description and default; `./git-cicd verify` passes.
- `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` byte-identical to before the epic.
- README states the changed rule, shows the form, says inputs changes need `generate` and a commit, and has the upgrade note; AGENTS.md says how a job is started by hand here; no doc mentions the JSON `inputs` field or `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` except the upgrade note.
- `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; the pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.
